title: Koh Chang’s Ghost Ship: What Remains?
requested_title: The Mystery Ghost Ship Left to Rot in a Thai Jungle (Koh Chang Part 2 — Exact GPS Coordinates)
visual_lock: Vertical 9:16 documentary travel mystery; humid Gulf of Thailand haze, emerald jungle, lagoon, weathered concrete and rust; naturalistic restrained teal/amber grade, slow stabilized camera. No supernatural apparitions, fabricated signage, trespassing, or invented present-day intact ship. Any intact Galaxy must be explicitly labeled archival reconstruction and matched to supplied licensed reference images.
reference_sheet_prompt: Create a documentary reference sheet for Koh Chang: (1) present-day southern Koh Chang lagoon and tropical shoreline, (2) a clearly labeled archival reconstruction of the former seven-deck Galaxy ship-hotel based only on supplied reference photographs, (3) a clean map panel locating Koh Chang, Trat, Thailand. Maintain realistic geography and muted emerald/teal/amber palette. No ghosts, logos, fabricated text, or implication the ship survives the 2024 fire. Use as consistent reference for all blocks.
important_factual_note: Important factual correction: The Galaxy ship-hotel was severely burned on 3 December 2024; a 2025 local update reports dismantling of its upper structure. Do not present the intact ship as currently standing. No current 2026 on-site inspection is available here; verify the present site, remnants and legal access before publication. HTMS Chang is a different ship: the US Naval History and Heritage Command dates the former LST-898's laying down to 15 October 1944 and commissioning to 29 December 1944; NavSource identifies it as ex-USS Lincoln County, 328 ft/100 m overall. PADI lists HTMS Chang as intentionally scuttled on 22 November 2012 to form an artificial reef, about 30 m to the seabed with a stated maximum depth of 34 m. Some dive listings report 117 m length; use the naval 328 ft specification and label dive depths approximate because local references differ. Never say HTMS Chang was sunk during WWII.

blocks.source_notes: Important factual correction: The Galaxy ship-hotel was severely burned on 3 December 2024; a 2025 local update reports dismantling of its upper structure. Do not present the intact ship as currently standing. No current 2026 on-site inspection is available here; verify the present site, remnants and legal access before publication. HTMS Chang is a different ship: the US Naval History and Heritage Command dates the former LST-898's laying down to 15 October 1944 and commissioning to 29 December 1944; NavSource identifies it as ex-USS Lincoln County, 328 ft/100 m overall. PADI lists HTMS Chang as intentionally scuttled on 22 November 2012 to form an artificial reef, about 30 m to the seabed with a stated maximum depth of 34 m. Some dive listings report 117 m length; use the naval 328 ft specification and label dive depths approximate because local references differ. Never say HTMS Chang was sunk during WWII.
